extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and wire-service journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Writing and assembling short wire-service news dispatches covering wartime events, human-interest items, and home-front reports for a general newspaper audience, using AP dateline/attribution conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline and date stamps
rubrics_metrics.description: Place the location and date prominently at the start of each dispatch (examples: 'NEW DELHI, INDIA, APRIL 24', 'ABOARD A SUBMARINE DEPOT SHIP SOMEWHERE IN THE MEDITERRANEAN, APRIL 21'). Also include sent or transmission dates where relevant (e.g., 'SENT APRIL 12').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use city/place, country (if foreign), and full date at the top of each short dispatch so readers immediately know where and when the report originates. Examples on page: multiple datelines (NEW DELHI, APRIL 24; BARRANQUILLA, COLOMBIA, APRIL 24) and explicit 'SENT APRIL 12'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Byline and reporter credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Credit the reporter or correspondent at the top or bottom of the dispatch (e.g., 'BY WES GALLAGHER', 'BY RICHARD G. MASSOCK').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the reporter's name to attribute original reporting; where multiple items appear on one page, each item may carry its own byline. Use consistent placement (commonly before the body or immediately after the dateline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency attribution and recording provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the news agency and provenance of material and recordings (e.g., the page uses '(AP)' after reports and phrases like 'THE BROADCAST, RECORDED IN NEW YORK BY THE ASSOCIATED PRESS').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When incorporating wire copy or material captured from other media (radio broadcasts, foreign dispatches), explicitly state the agency and where/when it was recorded to establish source reliability and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling of special status: delays, specials, advances
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark dispatches with their transmission status when appropriate (examples on page: '(DELAYED)-(AP)-' and 'AP SPECIAL ADVANCE FOR AMS OF SUNDAY, APRIL 25').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a report is delayed, is a special advance, or otherwise time-sensitive/exceptional, include an explicit tag so editors and readers understand timing and possible embargoes or special handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and labeling of anonymous sources / editor's note
rubrics_metrics.description: When material is based on an account from a source who must remain unnamed, identify that fact and use an editor's note where necessary (example: 'EDITOR’S NOTE: THE FOLLOWING ACCOUNT... WAS TOLD TO ... BY A PARTICIPANT WHO MUST REMAIN ANONYMOUS.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly flag anonymous-source material and provide an editor's explanatory note so readers understand the provenance and the reason for anonymity; preserve credibility by explaining limitations of attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise lede summarizing main facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Open each short dispatch with a tight lede that gives the essential facts up front (who/what/where/when/why), as in 'A SENIOR SUBMARINE OFFICER... REVEALED THAT ONE ROYAL NAVY SUBMARINE FLOTILLA ALONE HAS SUNK OR DISABLED 50 LARGE ENEMY SHIPS.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wire copy should front-load the most newsworthy facts in the first paragraph so readers (and editors) immediately grasp the significance; follow with supporting details and anecdotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute and distinguish material from other outlets (e.g., foreign radio/Italian/German broadcasts)
rubrics_metrics.description: When relaying reports originating from foreign radio or enemy/neutral broadcasts, explicitly attribute and, where applicable, indicate recording or transcription source (examples: 'A BERLIN BROADCAST, SAID...', 'AN ITALIAN BROADCAST SAID', 'THE ALGIERS RADIO SAID...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear which statements are claims from foreign broadcasts; avoid presenting them as verified facts without corroboration. Note when a broadcast was recorded in another city or by the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Segmented short-dispatch style for multiple locales and topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the page as a series of short, stand-alone dispatches each with its own dateline and often brief paragraphs covering different theaters (e.g., North Africa, New Guinea, Rio de Janeiro, Mexico City) and topics (military action, human-interest, ceremonies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use separate datelines and short paragraphs so diverse items can be read independently; mix battle reports, political developments and human-interest pieces but keep each item compact and self-contained for the wire-reader/editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit labeling of special reports and memorial/ceremonial coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag when coverage is thematic or commemorative (examples: 'AP SPECIAL ADVANCE', 'WAR AREA‘S FIRST AVENING BLOW DEDICATED TO THE MEMORY OF THE AMERICAN AIRMEN EXECUTED IN TOKYO', ANZAC/Easter ceremonies coverage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting on memorials, holidays, or commemorative events tied to the war, explicitly frame items so readers understand their ceremonial or symbolic nature; provide context linking them to current events.
